caption_review: None of the four captions merely repeats a title; each names the machine and frame, the series vocabulary, and the quantities a reader needs. The frame-137 and frame-146 captions give the saved residual, convergence, the marker shapes for all three fields (blue solid/filled solved, dark dashed/hollow EFIT, grey dash-dot/hollow physical image), the governed wall, the identical gauge-free contour levels with their values in Wb, the hollow secondary-saddle convention, and both the saved and the physical-image miss in centimetres. The attribution caption defines every row term including 'response' and 'held nodes', and states that sum and observed coincide without fitting, which the plotted marks show. The profiles caption names the shared knot grid. No caption is recorded as a finding.

findings.summary: In profiles.png the hollow grey 'prescribed knots' circles are drawn above both traces (zorder 6, markersize 6) at the same normalized-flux abscissae as the 4 pt solved triangles, so in the two FF' panels no solved triangle is visible at any knot: the blue trace reads as a bare line with grey circles sitting on it, while the legend advertises a triangle for that series. Both series remain separable by line style and the FF' disagreement is still visible, so nothing is concealed; the cost is that the fixed legend marker for 'solved extraction' does not appear in two of the four panels.

Within each frame figure the same grey carries two different series: the governed wall (line 166, solid 1.5 pt) and the physical-image field (dash-dot 2.6 pt with hollow diamonds). In the lower-X zoom both appear as nearby grey strokes, and the right-hand wall fragment is a plain grey polyline that a reader scanning the panel can take for the physical-image field before checking the dash pattern. The two do have separate legend entries and different line styles, so the picture is readable; the defect is that colour no longer names one component within the figure.

The strip under each frame panel renders the Python boolean directly, so the reader sees 'converged True' rather than 'converged: yes' or 'converged, residual 8.98e-12'. It reads as program output on an otherwise presentational figure, though the meaning is unambiguous.

The lower-X zooms are drawn at the same on-page width as the full poloidal panel while covering a window about 4.2 times smaller (a 0.36 m box against the full panel's 1.5 m range), and the window extent is stated nowhere: axes are off and the caption says only 'lower-X zoom'. The wall fragment at the right edge is the only geometric scale clue inside the zoom, so a reader comparing the two panels can over-read the size of the features in the zoom. The caption's miss in centimetres is what actually fixes the scale.
